react_result.final_narrative_text: Differential metabolomics analysis across three complementary enrichment paradigms reveals robust perturbation of glutathione-dependent detoxification and amino acid one-carbon metabolism. RaMP multi-DB ORA identifies three high-confidence pathway clusters with FDR < 0.005: the broad Reactome 'Metabolism' super-pathway (fold-enrichment 35.8, 4 hits), WikiPathways 'Trans-sulfuration, one-carbon metabolism and related pathways' (WP:WP2525, fold-enrichment 450, glutathione + phosphoserine), and 'Amino acid metabolism in triple-negative breast cancer cells' (WP:WP5213, fold-enrichment 1422). The m/z-direct mummichog method independently recovers 'Glycine, serine, alanine and threonine metabolism' (p=0.007, overlap 4/4) and 'Xenobiotics metabolism' (p=0.007) as top-ranked hits, both anchored by glutathione and phosphoserine. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA corroborates pantothenic acid enrichment in 'Pantothenic acid and CoA biosynthesis' (hsa00770, p=0.049) and phosphoserine in glycine-serine-threonine (hsa00260, p=0.080) and cysteine-methionine (hsa00270, p=0.080) pathways. The convergence of four input metabolites — glutathione, O-phospho-L-serine, pantothenic acid, and coumarin — across all three paradigm classes strongly implicates oxidative stress response and thiol-redox homeostasis as the primary biological axis of the treatment effect. Coumarin and benzo[a]pyrene diol epoxide in the input list are xenobiotic substrates whose biotransformation routes intersect with the glutathione conjugation machinery.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three enrichment paradigms (RaMP multi-DB ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and mummichog m/z-network) converged on glutathione and pantothenic acid as the dominant signals. RaMP ORA ranked REACT:R-HSA-1430728 (Metabolism) top at fdr 6.918e-05, with pantothenic acid, coumarin, glutathione, and phosphoserine as hits. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently ranked hsa00770 (Pantothenic acid pathway) first at p 0.0494, with pantothenic acid as the sole hit. Mummichog m/z-network independently ranked Glycine, serine, alanine and threonine metabolism (MUMM) first at p 0.00924, with glutathione and phosphoserine confirmed in the metabolites_hit list. Cross-paradigm consensus: pantothenic acid hits in RaMP and MetaboAnalystR; glutathione and phosphoserine hit together in RaMP (Amino acid metabolism in triple-negative breast cancer cells, WP:WP5213, fdr 6.918e-05) and separately in mummichog. The co-occurrence of glutathione and phosphoserine in the same serine-family pathway combined with pantothenic acid perturbation across vitamin-cofactor metabolism suggests a combined perturbation of one-carbon/amino-acid metabolism and CoA-related pathways.
